c: Ridgeback FC, a minor league soccer team in a mid-sized city
s: Ridgeback FC averages 2,100 fans per home game in a 6,000-seat stadium. The director of marketing wants to fill more seats for a mid-season match against the team's biggest rival and to attract families and college students.
The director of marketing (judge) wants you to explain how to promote the match, which communication channels to use for each audience, and how to coordinate the efforts.
p: Explain the nature of a promotional plan
Identify the elements of the promotional mix
Explain the use of social media for digital marketing
Participate in the design of collateral materials to promote special events
Coordinate activities in the promotional mix
n: Sets goals such as attendance, ticket sales and merchandise sales
Combines advertising, social media, partnerships and community outreach
Short videos, player features and shareable content
Posters, school flyers and ticket promotions
Consistent theme and timing across all channels
q: How would you promote the game to families differently than to college students?
What would you do if ticket sales are behind plan one week before the game?

c: Metro Arena, a 14,000-seat venue for concerts and sports
s: Metro Arena wants to sell more group tickets to businesses, schools and youth teams. Representatives often send a price list without learning what the group wants, and few groups convert.
The group sales manager (judge) wants you to explain how to find out a group's needs, present packages with benefits, and ask for the business.
p: Determine customer/client needs
Explain the selling process
Analyze product information to identify product features and benefits
Convert customer/client objections into selling points
Close the sale
n: Asks about group size, goal, budget and date
Builds a package: tickets, food, parking, recognition on the scoreboard
Explains benefits in terms of the group's goal, such as team building or fundraising
Responds to objections with alternatives and asks for a decision
q: The group leader says the date is not good for them. What do you do?
How do you follow up with a group that did not buy?

c: Pulse Sports Network, a regional sports media company
s: Pulse Sports Network's streaming audience has stopped growing. The company wants to understand which fans watch, what they want and why some stop subscribing.
The vice president (judge) wants you to explain how to collect and analyze fan information, what types of questions you would ask, and how the findings could shape marketing decisions.
p: Explain the nature of marketing research
Describe the use of surveys in collecting information
Interpret statistical findings
Translate research findings into actionable business recommendations
Explain ethical considerations in providing information
n: Uses surveys, interviews, subscriber data and social listening
Writes clear unbiased questions and chooses a representative sample
Compares segments and finds patterns in churn
Recommends actions: content, pricing, communication
Protects privacy and is honest in how results are presented
q: What would you do if the data showed fans leave because of the price?
How would you make sure survey respondents represent all of your fans?

c: Skyline Stadium, home of a professional baseball team
s: Skyline Stadium received many complaints this season about long concession lines, unclear seating information and unhelpful staff. A recent survey ranked guest experience below the league average.
The guest experience manager (judge) wants you to explain how to improve fans' experience, how staff should handle upset fans, and how to turn feedback into improvements.
p: Demonstrate a customer service mindset
Handle customer/client complaints
Describe the use of technology in customer relationship management
Reinforce service orientation through communication
Solicit feedback
n: Staff greet fans, give directions and anticipate needs
Listens, apologizes, solves or escalates quickly
Uses mobile ordering, app notifications and a feedback form
Trains staff and uses consistent messages
Collects, reviews and acts on feedback
q: A fan says the seat they paid for has an obstructed view. What do you do?
How would you motivate part-time game-day staff to deliver great service?

c: Champion Sports Group, which runs youth tournaments and camps
s: During last month's youth tournament, two parents argued with a referee and a volunteer felt overwhelmed and walked off. Social media posts criticized the event.
The event director (judge) wants you to explain how an event manager stays calm and responsible under pressure, how to handle conflict, and how to model ethical behavior for volunteers and staff.
p: Demonstrate self-control
Use conflict-resolution skills
Model ethical behavior
Treat others with dignity and respect
Take responsibility for decisions and actions
n: Stays calm, lowers voice, and takes the discussion to a quieter place
Listens, finds common ground and applies rules fairly
Sets expectations on sportsmanship and enforces them consistently
Treats volunteers and parents with respect
Owns the mistake and explains how it will be fixed
q: A parent is shouting at a volunteer. What do you do first?
How would you support a volunteer who is overwhelmed in the middle of an event?
